title: POST /users crashes (500) when a required field has a non-string value
property: invalid input (wrong-typed username/email/password) gets a 4xx, never an unhandled exception
expected: 400 Bad Request via bad_request(...), like the other validation failures in create_user
actual: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'encode' at app/models.py:135 set_password (500). Likewise username/email null -> IntegrityError, username/email list -> sqlite ProgrammingError at users.py:50/53.
evidence: create_user already validates input and returns 400 for missing fields and duplicates; the endpoint is the public unauthenticated sign-up, and the API convention (errors.py bad_request) is that client mistakes yield 4xx, not 500.

title: PUT /users/<id> crashes (500) when the JSON body is not an object
property: a malformed request body gets a 4xx, never an unhandled exception
input: authenticated PUT /api/users/1 with JSON body 0 (also null)
actual: TypeError: argument of type 'int' is not iterable at app/api/users.py:71 (500); same for POST /users at line 48
evidence: Handler does `'username' in data` assuming a dict without checking; API returns JSON 4xx errors for bad requests via bad_request().
